cutoff_window.rule: An explicitly visible publication or update date inside the 48-hour window is required; date-only values are retained only when the whole visible calendar date lies inside the window.

identity, authentication, authorization, credentials, and least privilege

wiki_and_federation_checked.routing_rule: Retain only security-specific boundaries, mitigations, evidence, and impacts locally; broad product entities belong in ai-wiki and general AI-assisted development practices belong in ai-dev-wiki.

source_collection_method.discovery: Public CVE and advisory-database searches, with linked public project advisory, patch, and release references where available.
source_collection_method.duplicate_check: Searched raw, raw/processed, docs/wiki, and both upstream topic indexes for retained CVE identifiers and named entities.

qualifying_findings.title: ChatCLI MCP OAuth resource-indicator origin validation error
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Published CVE record from VulnCheck, with a listed maintainer-hosted GitHub advisory, patch, and fixed release.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: ChatCLI v1.159.0 through before v1.215.2; MCP OAuth login and server-supplied Protected Resource Metadata resource indicator.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The published record says ChatCLI used server-supplied Protected Resource Metadata as an OAuth resource indicator without verifying that it matched the configured MCP server URL. A malicious MCP server could obtain a bearer token for another resource on the same authorization server and replay it there. The record lists v1.215.2 as the fixed release.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP OAuth metadata is a delegated-authority boundary. Client acceptance of unbound resource metadata can redirect bearer-token authority across resources.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: ChatCLI product background belongs in ai-wiki and general MCP client workflows belong in ai-dev-wiki; retain this OAuth resource-origin validation boundary locally.
follow_up_actions: During ingest, confirm the maintainer advisory and v1.215.2 release remediation wording before asserting deployment guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: mcp-go OAuth well-known metadata origin validation error
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public vulnerability-database publication; NVD record URL retained for later primary-record reconciliation.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: mark3labs/mcp-go before v1.2.1; OAuthHandler.fetchServerMetadata handling of well-known Protected Resource Metadata.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: Public vulnerability-database entries identify an origin-validation error in mcp-go OAuth metadata processing before v1.2.1. The issue concerns unvalidated well-known Protected Resource Metadata, making it an OAuth authority-binding control gap; v1.2.1 is identified as the fixed version.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP servers and clients use OAuth to authorize tool and resource access. Metadata-origin validation prevents a hostile server from steering delegated credentials toward an unintended protected resource.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: mcp-go SDK catalog and generic MCP implementation material belong in ai-wiki, and normal tool-governance practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki; retain this OAuth authority-binding flaw locally.
follow_up_actions: Obtain the maintainer advisory, patch commit, or v1.2.1 release notes before durable synthesis; retain the NVD URL as the canonical CVE-record check.

qualifying_findings.title: Dify Sandbox Run Handler hard-coded credentials
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Published CVE record from VulDB, corroborated by public vulnerability databases; no maintainer patch or fixed release was identified during collection.
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: langgenius Dify through 1.18.0 and 2.0.0-beta.2; Sandbox Run Handler api/configs/feature/__init__.py.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The published record reports hard-coded credentials in the Dify Sandbox Run Handler, says the attack can be launched remotely, and notes public exploit availability. The collected sources do not establish a fixed release.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: AI application sandboxes isolate model- and agent-triggered execution. Embedded credentials can collapse that control boundary and expose sandbox-backed services or data.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Dify product context belongs in ai-wiki and general application-building practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki; retain the sandbox credential boundary and missing-patch evidence locally.
follow_up_actions: Seek a maintainer advisory, issue, commit, or fixed release before deriving remediation; do not treat public-exploit language as evidence of active exploitation.
